title: Define multi-stage rollout authorization lattice and audit trail for model deployments
creator: Ava Patel
description: Purpose: establish a practical, auditable approval lattice (multi-role gating) and change-management workflow that governs model rollouts across canary, A/B, and shadow deployments. The lattice must be enforced in hosted, dedicated, and private (VPC) modes and integrate with RBAC, audit logging, and console UX. Scope includes: approval matrix definition, API and Console flows for submitting rollouts for sign-off, automated enforcement hooks (block/queue/notify), audit log schema and retention, and integration points for auto-rollback triggers tied to observability signals.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Approval lattice expressed as a config object that maps roles (PM, Data-Scientist, SRE, Security, Legal) to required sign-off types (explicit, advisory) and minimum approvers
A2: Console workflow to create a rollout request with required approvers visible and actionable from the UI
A3: API endpoints to submit/approve/revoke rollout requests with idempotent semantics and RBAC enforcement
A4: Audit logs emitted for every state transition (created, submitted, approved, rejected, scheduled, started, paused, rolled-back) with immutable metadata and linkable artifact references
A5: Auto-rollback policy hooks that trigger when configured SLO/metric thresholds cross (latency, error rate, quality regression) and are recorded as a remediation event in the audit log
A6: Documentation and runbook for on-call to handle hung approvals, emergency bypass (with elevated logging), and post-incident forensic queries
A7: End-to-end smoke test in a staging environment demonstrating canary->gradual->full rollout when approvals are granted, and immediate rollback when threshold breach occurs
notes_and_discussion: 2026-02-18: Kickoff — aligned with Eng, SRE, Security and Legal. Primary risk: inconsistent enforcement across Private deployments where customers manage control plane connectivity. Action: define a 'lightweight enforcement mode' that emits guidance and audit logs even when enforcement is delegated.

2026-02-22: Technical scoping with runtime team (ENG-1924). Proposed approach: central approval service in control plane for hosted/dedicated; declarative policy bundle for Private with webhook callbacks for approval decisions.

2026-02-25: RBAC mapping discussion — Security recommends introducing 'approval groups' rather than individual role-based signoffs to simplify enterprise SSO mappings. Follow-up: sample mapping doc in Confluence.

2026-02-26: Decision: audit log schema will include: event_id, rollout_id, actor, actor_identity_provider, action, before_state, after_state, artifacts (PR/PRD links), metrics_snapshot, and correlation_id. Retention: 1 year by default; customizable by enterprise customers.

2026-02-27: UX mock review — two-button flow in Console (Request approval -> Add reviewers -> Submit). Notifications via email and Slack (integration). Marcus to produce hi-fi mocks (Figma link below).

2026-02-28: Auto-rollback integration — runtime will expose a 'rollback-vote' API that the approval service can call when metric thresholds breach. Vote will record reason and trigger rollback if quorum (configurable) reached. Edge-case: simultaneous manual unfreeze by approver should be blocked for 10 minutes after auto-rollback; include in runbook.
2026-03-01: Security review kickoff scheduled; Legal asked for evidence capture (signed approvals + artifacts) for regulated customers. This affects data stored in audit logs and retention policies.
